newsitem.title: UK: Abbas Gokal found guilty in UK BCCI fraud trial.
newsitem.headline: Abbas Gokal found guilty in UK BCCI fraud trial.

text.p: Abbas Gokal, former chairman of the Gulf Group the biggest single borrower from the failed Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) was convicted on Thursday by a London court of conspiring to account falsely and of conspiracy to defraud, the Serious Fraud Office said.

The SFO said in a statement that Gokal, 61, had with BCCI officials "masterminded a massive fraud totalling approximately $1.2 billion". BCCI collapsed in 1991, costing many people their savings. The SFO, which investigates and prosecutes major financial fraud in Britain said this was the biggest fraud in banking history and the largest ever fraud trial.

Chris Dickson, the SFO lawyer heading the BCCI inquiry team, said Gokal's actions had "brought despair to hundreds of thousands of ordinary people who put their savings into BCCI. They are proof, if proof is needed, that human misery is the real cost of fraud".

The SFO said it had found documents signed by Gokal in a London safe deposit box which showed that he and his two brothers owned and controlled the companies involved in the fraud. It said the sums he received from BCCI supported Gokal's lavish lifestyle.

Gokal fled from his company base in Geneva, Switzerland to Pakistan in 1992 after his shipping and trading group Gulf collapsed. He was arrested by German police in Frankfurt airport in July 1994 when the plane landed on a flight from Karachi. He was extradited to Britain and has been in custody since he arrived in December 1994.

The conviction of Gokal, whose trial at the Old Bailey last September, will be seen as a much-needed boost to the SFO. The office's record is under constant media scrutiny following several high-profile cases in which it failed to secure convictions after lengthy and expensive trials.
He is expected to be sentenced on May 6.
